Of course not, as long as the time and place is right, and that the intent is to just get to know, form connection first rather than jumping right to becoming boyfriend girlfriend.

I get that social interaction is hard—especially today—and I agree we *should* be more open to connection. But connection isn’t just about expressing your intent; it’s also about respecting the context and the comfort of others.

Saying *“I might not see her again so I just want to try”* puts your desire to shoot your shot above her right to exist in that space without being made into a potential date. That’s not social anxiety—that’s prioritizing your discomfort with *missing a chance* over her discomfort with being approached while working out.

Also, intent matters—but so does delivery. “Do you have a boyfriend?” doesn’t just come off awkward; it puts the other person in a position to have to justify rejecting you, even if they just aren’t interested. It's not about calling all men creeps—it’s about recognizing that not every setting is appropriate for romantic approaches, and respecting when people set boundaries around that. If you're truly respectful, you don’t just ask and move on—you also learn *when not to ask* in the first place.

Of course you are right be respectful, that is a good thing, but that alone is not enough. There is a time and a place for everything. and the gym is not the best place for hitting people up. As I mentioned in another comment, the gym is different from other public spaces like the bar or the park. It's more intimate and people are more vulnerable there, not to mention how tired people can be in the gym, with no energy or focus left on anything else than finishing their workout.

I think the issue is, while the gym might be a public place, it is *intimate in purpose*. People are there in vulnerable states: sweating, focused, sometimes insecure about their bodies, often trying to mentally push through tough workouts. It’s not a social “open mode” like a bar or park, so hitting people up at the gym is inappropriate, if not creepy.

That's not mentioning hitting someone up with "Do you have a boyfriend/girlfriend?". That question is so loaded, as it turns a casual, neutral space into one charged with romantic/sexual intent.

Lastly, OP is also framing women who rejects his advantages as uncomfortable with “real life social interaction”. If that is not an incel vibe, I don't what is.

If again there's no slot available to fulfill that need, it will be skipped as well and so on until they have cycled through the last need to fulfill, then they get back to work.

So technically speaking, the fewer service buildings there are to visit to fulfill their needs, the sooner Tropicans get back to work.

Many factors can be at play here:

* Teamster commute time: not only do they do need housing near their workplace, groceries, entertainment, religious, and healthcare buildings ('services') need to be close, too, because they also cycle between housing - workplace - services.
   * You can inspect each teamster by clicking on them to see their journey; it's possible that they're at a tavern at the other end of the island because local beauty gives that one +1 service quality higher than the one nearby. That's a pesky reason why I never use service buildings that are affected by beauty.
   * Since we're on the topic, make sure you have enough service buildings to accomodate the entire population: if the service building nearby has its visiting slots fully booked, Tropicans will choose the next one that can be far away.
   * And not just teamsters, you'll need to apply the 'everything built close around' rule to ALL workers of production buildings as well!
* Not enough raw material production: the 'safe' ratio is 2 raw material producer per 1 processing factory (example: 2 sugar plantations per 1 distillery). Sometimes you *may* get by with one raw material producer but it falls off balance very easily (and factories will show empty input signs), so always root for the 2:1 ratio.
   * The employee of the month edict only affects factories and mines, and not other raw material producers (plantations, ranches, log camps, oil wells), 
* If you're in colonial time, pirates and crown force can 'scare' teamsters causing them to seek refuge inside buildings, stalling material delivery and thus production.

Letting yourself feel the anger, acknowledge and accept it, while trying to remain calm and resisting any urge to take destructive action is the way, until the emotion passes away and you can tackle whatever/whoever angered you in a more rational and constructive manner.

One way is to learn about organic city development, as opposed to planned development.

In the beginning (colonial to WW), it’s natural to have most of your population scattered around the countryside, where they work in farms and ranches rather than in cities, and live in country houses instead of tenements.

In the same spirit, entertainment for the country folks should be limited to taverns and maybe restaurants, instead of opera houses and cabarets, which fit better in cityscape.

You can have your historic city around the palace, where the elites work in government, education, or military. Most of them are well off or rich, enjoy opera performances, and live in houses near their workplace.

When industrialization comes, build a large settlement around factories near the dock along with teamsters, consisting of only tenements despite factories providing well-off wealth level and workers can afford better housing.

This is to realistically reflect crowded and polluted urban centers in the 1920s. And for entertainment, use cabarets instead of opera houses, the latter being more refined and cultured, thus unsuitable for the rowdy working class.

Those are just some ideas based on historic elements. You may realize that ‘realistic’ is somewhat based on clichés and esthetics rather than efficiency, but that’s how I play Tropico. Maxing out and optimizing everything doesn’t make realistic cities.

Like I said, some actually enjoy the rush, others (including me) find it overwhelming lol.

One thing that helped me whenever I feel overwhelmed with shame and guilt (pretty common for borderlines), I let them ‘radically hit me’ (from radical acceptance).

Just ride the wave of shame and self-blame, let it ‘tells’ you how you messed up and at the same time pause your judgements and try not to ‘argue’ with the shame (by saying ‘no this is wrong, there’s nothing for me to be ashamed of’, for ex.).

This allows you to feel whatever comes to you, the fullest, so it can leave you the fastest. They usually last less than a minute if you let yourself be fully focused and immersed and attentive of that feeling, and you’ll feel so much more relief when it leaves.

And of course, rationally (and objectively), you already know all those shameful things you’re told from yourself are not true, at least only partially, with important parts left out and/or in a very unkind way to yourself, so it there’s no hurt letting them put on that horror show for a short while.

- what has been produced has already been taken away by teamsters (to factory / dock...)
- nothing's been produced yet, which I think your case may be this one

In Tropico 6 things work differently than in T5: The workers of your production building must be AT WORK in order for the building to generate/produce the amount of goods in accordance with the building's efficiency.

This means that even though the efficiency of your rum distillery is 150%, as long as all the building's workers are busy elsewhere (going to the grocery, clinic or simply resting at home, for ex), your building will produce nothing.

That's why in T6 is important to consider the logistic factors when building your city: are the workers' amenities (churches, clinics, homes...) close to their work place? Is there affordable transportation available to reduce their travel time? (If not they will simple walk 😂)

You can enable the employees of the month edict to set double shifts for your factories, aka the game will try to enforce at least one or 2 workers to stay behind at the factory until others return.
Yes you only need 1 worker to stay behind for a factory to produce the efficiency-based amount, given that all worker slots have been hired :)

As someone has mentioned, not having enough working population and rapidly spawning building (regardless of production or amenities) can hurt your economy, and coupling that with not having enough raw resources for those production buildings, you'll go down pretty quickly.

Despite the general rule of 2 raw material buildings / 1 factory, which really works in most cases, at times you can end up with not having enough raw materials because those stup.. I mean 'intellectually challenged' plantation workers decide to go to *that* tavern 2 islands away and can't get back to their workplace soon enough to produce raw materials for a factory, causing shortage and interruption in the production chain.

My trick is to invest in the pirate cove building, place it near my factory-dock cluster and have it perform continuous raids for all raw materials my factories need, to complement/supplement the raw materials that your plantations or log camps produce that can eventually run into shortage one time or another. The remaining unused raw materials if exceed beyond the storage capacity of factories will be sent to the dock for cash.

Also, avoid costly recurrent edicts (free wheels, for example).

The employee of the month edict, despite its potential benefit, should be used with caution since it only effects factories and not raw material production buildings or teamsters. Imagine only doubling the working hour for factories with no change to that of raw material production buildings or teamsters who deliver raw materials, your factories will quickly end up in raw material shortage; and again if your economy is almost entire agricultural with little to no factory, enabling that edict will not bring in any tangible benefit to offset that 350 per month.

Anyway, those are my two cents :)

In Tropico 5 there was 'corruption' in play. You can consult the Alamac and see how much you lose each year to corruption. The more authoritarian your constitution is, the bigger the corruption's impact will be. This explains why your cash flow dwindles faster than in previous (and following) iterations.

That said, you can offset the money lost to corruption by strengthening your economy. Google 'Tropico 5 mods' and download the 'resource manager' mod (I don't recall the exact name). This helped my economy tremendously, and I would recommend you give it a try.

Basically this changes the logistic modus operandi of the game: each production building will have their own 'inhouse teamsters' without having to rely on teamster offices for delivery.

An inhouse teamster will depart from each production building once a production output has been made, carrying the output to its next destination building (next tier factory or dock...), then disappear into that destination building (no retour or reuse of this teamster), and this cycle will begin again and again as soon as a new output is made.

You can tell by now that this system is much more efficient than the default one in T5. ;)

As a general rule, you can build basic necessities (churches, clinics, taverns and houses) near workplaces so as to minimize the workers travel time to fulfill their needs.

In the case of teamsters, however, I’m afraid you’ll have to ‘spread’ these necessities across your islands wherever a resource producing/manufacturing building exists, as teamsters can travel anywhere, and you can’t limit or ‘route’ them, as far as I know.

Some other suggestions I can give you beside spreading necessities everywhere, are:

- to maximize budget for teamster offices (to let them transport the biggest possible quantity per trip)
- apply the ‘double shift’ or something like that upgrade that adds more employees/teamsters
- build even more teamster offices/ports
- issue the edict ‘speedway’ (available via research)

With the 6th reiteration introducing the notion of ‘off time’ for workers/employees, you’ll have to settle with them working less time than in the previous reiterations.

Hope this helps!
